title: Music in the Billy Mack show and reading music
summary: He describes accompanying chorus, dancers and singers, Mack's songs, and how little he could read then.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, music for the chorus, the dance bar, and tap dance music, and music for the singer. Then the comedian named Henry Reno, he, you know, we should play some songs and things for him. And Billy Mack, well, he had all his own songs. Hard Luck was one of his songs. Yeah. Black But Sweet Old God. That's when you made a record. And Miss Mack, and had another lady with her by the name of Mary Evans, and they did a number by the call of Bear. It was a beautiful thing, too, Bear. That was the name of her, Bear, but the way they sang it, huh?
Bear, Bear, Biddlem. Yeah, that's what's the name of the song, Bear, Bear, Bear, Biddlem. Oh, it was really good, so. I did all right.
Did you say music in the show, did you have to read music, or did they just read everything?

Well, they did have a little music scratched out, but I wasn't such a good reader then. This fellow trombone player, he was a mighty good musician, Wilbert Parrish. He had a brother named Sidney Parrish, you might have heard of him.
